topic: B2B Thought Leadership and Content Strategy
headline: Content Marketing Strategy
keyNotes: You can't just keep creating new content without looking back; one article title warns about "content debt," which means old content needs maintenance, or it can become a problem.

Making great content is only half the battle; how you get it to people (your "distribution strategy") is just as important. An article title asks, "Why Your Distribution Strategy Is Stunting Your Audience Growth," meaning if you don't share it well, your audience won't grow.

Even with all the places to share things online, having content on your own website ("owned content") is still a powerful strategy. One title says, "Your Website, Your Rules: Why Owned Content Still Wins," because you control it completely.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a big deal for content, impacting how it's found and even how you plan for the future. Titles like "Top Strategies to Get Your Content Cited by AI" show that understanding AI is key to getting your content seen.

While numbers and analytics are useful, they don't always give the full picture; real conversations are still vital. An article title highlights, "What Data Can't Tell You (But a Conversation Can)," suggesting that talking to people directly reveals deeper insights.
question: The article mentions that 'a better strategy is emerging' beyond traditional content marketing and that 'what data can't tell you, a conversation can.' In your own work, where do you find yourself relying too much on numbers, and where could a simple conversation reveal a more effective path forward?
